title: Priming tether workbench — personal rollout notes
body:
Purpose:
This is my personal scratchpad for the upcoming model flip + priming run (embedding-v3 -> embed-v3-quant). Focus: per-tenant priming, tethered ramp, and a conservative unpin strategy so we don’t disturb heavy enterprise tenants. Not an official runbook — refine and push to the team doc after one dry run.

TL;DR (two lines):
- Do a tiny shadow priming wave (0.5% traffic, target warm buckets) for 90m, validate latency and embedding drift; if green, advance to tethered 5% for 4h.
- Pin heavy tenants for 24h and gate them into a manual approval list before unpin.

Objectives:
- Ensure cache warmup reduces p99 token latency for short seqs (<128) by at least 10% compared to baseline.
- No >1.5x increase in error rate on any tenant during tether window.
- Detect embedding distribution drift (cosine mean shift) >0.06 and trigger hold.

Constraints / context:
- This is a quantized variant (embed-v3-quant) — CPU offload and new kernel path.
- Dedicated pools in us-west1 and eu-west1 only for initial run.
- Several enterprise tenants are flagged "sensitive-priming" in tenant DB and must remain pinned unless manual approval granted.

Quick checklist (pre-run):
- [ ] Confirm infra autoscaler warmup knobs (autoscale.min=2, burst=1) with infra oncall (Diego).
- [ ] Create canary cohort: small set of tenants + synthetic primer traffic (see synthetic script below).
- [ ] Update routing policy: route 0.5% -> embed-v3-quant (shadow/logging enabled).
- [ ] Add metric taps: per-tenant latency, per-tenant error rate, embedding-cosine-distribution, kv-cache-hit-rate.
- [ ] Notify CS + SRE channels (#cs-alerts, #sre-priming) with ETA and rollback plan.

Priming traffic recipe (quick):
- Synthetic script: tools/priming/generate_primer.py --tenant-list small-cohort.csv --pattern short-ctx=90% --seed=stable --qps=5
- Primer load: steady 5 qps per tenant for 45 minutes, then taper for 15 minutes. Purpose: populate prefix KV and reuse embedding cache.

Run phases:
1) Shadow priming (0.5% global traffic, logging only) — 90m
   - Verify: no increase in 95/99 latency by >20% per tenant, error rate <0.5% absolute.
   - Telemetry to watch: kv-cache-hit-rate uptrend, model-inference-duration median trending down.
2) Tethered canary (5% traffic, controlled cohorts) — 4h
   - Pin heavy tenants (list below) remain on embed-v3. Toggle for others.
   - Monitor every 5m, have manual hold button ready.
3) Gradual unpin wave (by tenant risk group) — multi-day, docs to follow.

Pinned tenants (manual list — DO NOT AUTOMATICALLY UNPIN):
- tenant-alpha-pro
- tenant-enterprise-brisbane
- tenant-zeta-health

Telemetry & failure criteria (immediate hold triggers):
- Per-tenant error rate increase >1.0 percentage point over baseline for 2 consecutive 5m windows -> HOLD
- Global p99 latency degradation >30% for 10m -> HOLD and rollback to previous routing policy
- Embedding drift: cosine mean shift >0.06 for any cohort of >1000 samples -> HOLD and snapshot examples -> notify ML lead
- KV cache hit drop >25% vs baseline (indicates cache bypass) -> investigate kernel path, consider returning to embed-v3

Rollback quick actions (fast path):
- Step 1: Flip route back to embed-v3 via routing-control api: curl -X POST ${ROUTER}/routes/flip -d '{"model":"embed-v3"}' (ops-only token)
- Step 2: Abort current priming job and mark cohort as "requires postmortem"
- Step 3: Notify #sre-priming and create incident (use template: Incident-Priming-Template).
- Step 4: Keep logs and snapshots, collect 5k embedding pairs (old vs new) for drift analysis.

Post-run validation (after tether window):
- Aggregated report: per-tenant latency percentiles, error rates, kv-cache-hit-rate, embeddings drift histogram (attach).
- Hold decision matrix: success if all: median latency delta <= +10%, p99 <= +20%, error rate delta <= +0.5% and drift <= 0.04.
- If success: plan a staged unpin schedule (low-risk tenants -> 24h -> monitor -> next group).

Notes-to-self / loose ideas:
- Could try "micro-priming" (small cohort primed for 12h before tether) to test warmup decay curves.
- Consider synthetic traffic that mirrors enterprise slow-session long-context patterns. Right now primer is short-ctx heavy.
- Evaluate gated quantization profile for high-entropy inputs — maybe fallback to full-precision for queries with >200 tokens. Open question: do we have an easy predicate?

Open questions / followups:
- Who owns tenant "tenant-zeta-health" escalation? (asked Priya)
- Need infra signoff on burst policy change — ping Diego for 2026-03-02 EOD
- Do we want automatic roll-forward on success after 24h or require manual approval? my vote: manual for enterprise.

Housekeeping commands (refs):
- Check live cohorts: ./tools/ops/list_cohorts.sh --env prod --cohort priming-02
- Flip route dry-run: curl -H "X-DRY-RUN:1" -X POST $ROUTER/routes/plan -d '{"target":"embed-v3-quant","fraction":0.005}'
- Collect embedding samples: python tools/telemetry/collect_embeddings.py --cohort priming-02 --max 10000 --out s3://redwood-ops/priming/sam/

Draft timeline (proposal):
- Day 0: shadow priming (0.5%) — small cohort — confirm no regression (90m)
- Day 1: tethered 5% (4h) — expand cohort, pin heavy tenants
- Day 2: analysis, decide unpin schedule
- Day 3+: staged unpin-by-risk group (low->med->high) with 24h observation windows

Quick risks I am worried about:
- Hidden perf cliffs on long-context sessions (we are testing short-heavy primer)
- Edge-case kernel fallback that silently increases CPU usage on node leading to noisy neighbour effects
- Telemetry sampling too low for small tenants — might miss regressions (increase sample rate for those tenants during tether)

TODOs (me):
- [ ] Finalize small-cohort tenant CSV and hand to Diego by 2026-03-03
- [ ] Add additional long-ctx primer pattern and test locally
- [ ] Draft a short email to CS with candidate unpin timeline and link to this doc

If anything looks off during run, default action = HOLD + rollback. No automated optimistic roll-forward unless explicitly approved.

End notes: this felt useful as a one-pager for my ops shift. After run, I will convert into canonical canary-playbook entry and add concrete metric thresholds to the routing service config.

-- Sam
